steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Film genre is a categorisation system that groups films sharing similar narrative patterns, visual styles, themes and emotional effects. | Key Fact: Steve Neale argued that genre depends on both repetition of conventions and difference and variation to sustain audience interest. | Key Fact: The 'repertoire of elements' describes the set of conventions that characterise a genre — setting, character types, iconography, narratives and themes. | Key Fact: Iconography refers to the visual symbols and recurring images associated with a genre: cowboy hats in westerns, spaceships in sci-fi, masks in horror.
